comment: Versioned, append-only MIDI phrase corpus (docs/plan.md section 4.8). See README.md for the versioning rules, the full per-phrase authoring specification, and what every field below means. corpusVersion is an integer that increments whenever a phrase is ADDED; existing phrases and their bytes never change, so a render filename carrying a corpus version identifies exactly one set of MIDI files. Version 1 is the P1 set (01, 03, 05, 07); version 2 appends the P2 set (02, 04, 06, 08) at Task P2.8. The P1 entries below are BYTE-FOR-BYTE what version 1 carried, including the fields they do not set: numStrings and allocationMode default to the single-string full-range configuration cnpg_render used through P1, which is what keeps a frozen phrase entry rendering the configuration its own `exercises` field describes.

phrases.description: Full-range single notes: a chromatic run from MIDI 21 (A0) to 108 (C8), then five sustained anchors left to ring for 3 s each, then one pitch struck at six velocities.
phrases.exercises: Decay character across the whole range, tuning across the whole range, velocity response, silence hygiene between notes.

phrases.description: Same-pitch replucks (accelerating), an ascending legato slur, a descending legato slur, a fast trill, and same-pitch replucks on a long low string. Rendered in the default retrigger mode only; the per-mode variant renders land in Task P2.8 with DamperJunction.
phrases.exercises: RetriggerMode::Physical semantics -- repluck over a ringing string, and a pitch-changing retrigger -- plus pop-free note transitions.

phrases.description: ABUSE. Aggressive +/-2-semitone bends on the lowest playable note (MIDI 21), overlapping with replucks; then 5.5 Hz vibrato on MIDI 28; then a slow dive and return on MIDI 40 with a repluck at the bottom; then a 3 Hz full-range triangle wheel back on MIDI 21. Wheel messages are 5 ms apart throughout every ramp.
phrases.exercises: Bend cleanliness at the extremes of the range the string rails are sized for, click-freedom under continuous wheel motion, retriggers landing mid-bend.

phrases.description: ABUSE. Four long held notes, one per sweep section, each with a mid-note repluck; the sidecar sweeps pickup position, then pickup resonance and Q, then triode drive, then the material morph, while the note rings.
phrases.exercises: Pluck-position audibility, click-free and zipper-free parameter motion mid-note, triode drive character (within the static-waveshaper caveat), abuse survival.

phrases.description: Seven strummed open-position chords (E, A, D, G, C, Am, Em) held to ring; then the low E held under twelve staccato notes above it; then the near-unison pair (MIDI 45 on string 1 and MIDI 46 on string 0, first held together and then string 0 alone against string 1 at rest), which the coupling comparison configs detune into a 25-cent pair; then seven simultaneous notes on six strings, so the seventh steals.
phrases.exercises: Six real voices on one loaded bridge: fingering plausibility, sympathetic shimmer, chord stability below the limiter ceiling, near-unison mode locking (ADR 0007 D5 criterion 4), and the steal policy.

phrases.description: ABUSE. Eighth-note and sixteenth-note chugging on the open low E, power-chord chugs, a long-short-short gallop, a re-strike gap ladder at 5/12/21/53/100 ms after each note-off, and chugs resolving into a let-ring. Rendered with the damper near the bridge and only partly absorbing, which is what a palm mute is on this instrument.
phrases.exercises: Fast retriggers into a partially absorbing damper: short PITCHED thumps rather than clicks, no energy buildup between hits, no machine-gun sameness, and whether a fresh attack masks the state clear a re-strike performs (checklist item 21).

phrases.description: Chords under CC64: one chord held past its key releases; a second chord arriving over the first while the pedal still holds it; a re-strike under the pedal that must survive the pedal-up; a slow half-pedal sweep across the 64 threshold in both directions; and a six-string chord released by one pedal-up.
phrases.exercises: CC64 deferral end to end -- notes ringing past their note-offs, six dampers landing on one sample, a re-strike cancelling a pending release, and one clean transition per threshold crossing rather than a stutter.

phrases.description: Ten notes (MIDI 40 then MIDI 45), each rung for 0.9 s and then released and left to ring for 2.9 s with the damper sitting on a node. The sidecar steps damperPosition01 to 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/5 and finally to the default 0.15 before each note, always inside a silent gap, so the damper is already AT the node when the note-off engages it. ONE string, and the tap off the midpoint, both for measurement reasons stated in README.md: on six coupled strings the neighbours ring at exactly the partials under test, and a tap at the default 0.5 sits on a node of every even partial.
phrases.exercises: Harmonic behaviour of a point damper: p = 1/2 suppresses the fundamental and leaves the octave, p = 1/3 leaves the twelfth, and the 0.15 control is the position with no low-order node on it.
